justifications.c1: Only US per-rat feed-loss figures ($6.90 to $25 per rat per year; Poultry Site, Mississippi State Extension), with no UK per-farm figure and no £ cost of a failed Red Tractor audit (recorded not found).
justifications.c2: CRRU requires permanent outdoor bait points to be re-inspected at least every four weeks (BPCA, search-confirmed) and Red Tractor requires at least quarterly site surveys; but CRRU steers farms away from permanent baiting, so how many farms carry the 4-weekly duty is unknown.
justifications.c3: Paper bait plans with inspection dates are documented, and council rodent contracts cost about £300–£345 a year for 4–8 visits (Gwynedd, search-confirmed at £250–£275 + VAT; Tameside); farmer labour is unquantified, and a sensor would not remove the contractor's bait visits.
justifications.c4: Red Tractor requires a bait plan with bait-point inspection and replenishment dates, kept for 2 years after changes (Red Tractor VC.b, search-confirmed), and CRRU stewardship conditions apply at point of sale; no non-conformity statistics or enforcement cases were found.
justifications.c5: The payer is 'the person with responsibility for vermin management' (farmer, farm manager or contractor); no job advert or budget evidence, and the benchmark farm pest spend is only ~£300 a year.
justifications.c6: Merchants sit inside the CRRU point-of-sale audit, Killgerm and BPCA reach pest professionals, and Pestfix sells a TrapSensor 12-month data plan (title only); no evidence that farm-visiting pest controllers or merchants sell connected bait monitoring to farms.
justifications.c7: Crowded and commoditising: Victor VLINK, Bell iQ ($38.30 station; app made free), EverSmart ($767.60 for 10), Trap-Alert ($535 + $39.50/month), SensorWorks ($195), Rentokil PestConnect and Anticimex SMART; the only gap is the CRRU/Red Tractor record format, evidenced by absence.
justifications.c8: Visit detection is off the shelf (EverSmart PIR, LoRaWAN), but the core bait-take estimate is still at research or patent stage (EMSD wish-list, RatSpy ±15%), an unproven sensing method.
justifications.c9: A recurring 4-weekly inspection duty and 2-year bait-plan retention, plus Trap-Alert's $39.50/month plan and Pestfix's data plan, but Bell making its app free and ~£300 farm pest budgets weaken the subscription case.
justifications.c10: CRRU barn-owl residue monitoring and BPCA trade items (about wildlife, not farmer pain) and article titles on passing audits; no forum thread, audit statistic or enforcement case showing missed bait records.

weakest: The money is tiny and US-sourced (dollars per rat per year, ~£300 farm pest budgets), and the bait-consumption sensing the concept relies on is not yet a proven off-the-shelf method.
